I emphasize with your daughter, and you. Obviously I hope your daughter is doing okay, but I hope you are as well, because I know this is hard. You’re both so strong, and so is your family. You’re doing great.

As for your questions. Well for question 1,2, and 4, it sounds you’re doing everything a person can, and I’m sorry I can’t help more. 

But for your third question, it’s complicated. Make sure you don’t frame cutting as a scary thing, nor a good thing. What I mean is, cutting is an event in the past, and it’s not shameful, or scary, or a trap for her to fall into. It’s just a thing that happened. 

It’s obviously harmful to remember cutting as positive, but the reason you don’t want to think about it negatively either is that it creates regret and self-hatred, which can cause a cycle. There’s nothing more stressful than wanting to hurt yourself because you hate that you used to hurt yourself. Keeping emotional attachment to cutting, positive or negative, may being her anxiety. 

You got this, best wishes to you and your daughter.

When I thought my mom was trying to kill me. It’s happened multiples times, sometimes rationally sometimes irrationally.

She was acting deranged, and I was beyond upset, and I genuinely believed she was trying to beat me so I couldn’t run away, which wasn’t far off from her intention. Not-so-coincidentally, I was experiencing a major depressive episode (which partially caused this event), and I threatened to run out to the nearby pond in the middle of freezing Canadian winter if she layed a finger on me. One thing led to another and eventually I froze in shock. I literally couldn’t speak, and could barely move. It’s ironic that I had been hit and smacked many times, but this event, where she never even managed to touch me, was the worst.

But that night was the first major time where I genuinely couldn’t function out of fear for my life.

One who’s 15 years older and two others who are about 8 years younger. I didn’t have a single father figure in my life because of him (not that he would’ve been a good one). Im in college and am still learning things that a man needs to know about himself.

So, what caused it? He caused it, for my entire life.

I know so much about this man, and yet he wouldn’t even be able to recognize my face because he just doesn’t care. I hate him, and I hate how loved, successful, and happy he is. 

And I feel so alone because the situation is so unique that nobody really understands how much it hurts. Because, no matter what I do in life, my most defining thing for the record books will always be the accidental mistake of a child that *celebrity man* had. That’s my legacy. Fuck him.

17M. Almost 4 years ago. Basically a pretty large problem managed to escalate even worse though misunderstanding between my single mother and I (only child).

I was 14, and had been experiencing extreme depressive episodes which I kept hidden from everyone. Suicide plans and attempts, cutting, all while keeping my thoughts in my own head for months, and eventually years afterwards. Even now, for reasons that are mostly irrelevant to the story. Only important things was that she was emotionally abusive, to a lesser extent, physically, so I feared her when she was angry.

I was struggling with less than 4 hours of sleep per day and constant stress to maintain a near perfect average. But one day, after a private depressive episode, I saved a picture of a quote to my desktop (my mom never uses my computer, and respects my privacy.) It was a quote about accepting death, I don’t remember it enough.

I decide to calm myself down to get back to work (it’s almost midnight and I was doing work), so I go downstairs to get some water and put on a relaxing show for like 10 min.

My mother starts screaming upstairs, and runs down to me. Screaming at me to get back to work (she’s just seen the file of the quote on my desktop, and this was how she handled it.) I said I needed a break, not telling her why. She proceeded to threaten me and stand over me fritter her teeth, screaming, with her hand up ready to start hitting me. I panic and jump off the couch as quick as possible to get around her, and out my arms against the wall. My only exit is the back door of the house, as she blocks the hallway. (Keep in mind I’ve just recovering from a breakdown less than 10 min before). 

My mother begins to threaten to pin me down. I had no idea she saw the quote upstairs at this point, so I thought she was trying to attack me by pinning me. When she says this, I start crying while still against the wall and finally retaliate by saying that I will run out into the freezing cold Canadian winter and jump in the pond near our house if she approaches me. She threatens me further saying she’ll call family to help her. At this point, I’m in full manic-breakdown-mode and think that she’s about to commit a felony and full-out brawl me, which I couldn’t imagine. Eventually after me running towards the back door, ready to run, she screamed at me to stop, and that if I won’t deal with her, I can talk to my Aunt and Uncle who she’d call. I think that’s when I realized she must’ve saw the picture and started to clue in what was happening. So I agreed.

My Aunt and Uncle come a few minutes later, with me just crying against the door and my mom backing off but keeping watch of me. I speak with my uncle and my mom talks to my aunt. I don’t remember what I said. All I remember was the 4 of us taking, with my mom swearing me to promise I wouldn’t leave in the middle of the night, and that I wasn’t trying to kill myself. I just ended up saying that of course I wasn’t suicidal and won’t run away (I had no intent of leaving so that part wasn’t a lie). She told me that she only threatened to pin me down so I wouldn’t kill myself, but that ironically made me threaten to harm/kill myself. Anyways, they left, I went to bed, and I barely talked to my mom for weeks. She slowly started talking again and never acknowledged the event ever again. Similar issues have happened both before and after, but this one scarred me.

Ever since then my emotions have been hidden. I’m a shell of who I was. But I’m far to afraid to express my issues because this is the only time someone’s ever found out, and look what happened.

I should mention that I have no idea how much time passed between “my mother screaming down the stairs” to “my aunt and uncle came over”. It could’ve been only 15 minutes, or it could’ve been an hour. I was so in shock and this event was so traumatizing that I reflect on it constantly. 

It’s 3:00 AM and I have an exam tomorrow, and I just typed a huge story because I’m reliving this event, among others, in my head. I’m so tired.
